solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fine coat on reflection, and frill

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things the wrong way round, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
an animal's coat is its fur

explanation.surface: A dandy admires his fine coat in the mirror, complete with a frill.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole of 'Fine coat' is turned round, not just the coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruff is a stiff pleated collar, a type of frill worn round the neck.

clue.text: Training in sensitive topic that's to be covered as fast as possible

definitions.text: that's to be covered as fast as possible

parts.note: race is a sensitive subject in discussion
a training course

explanation.surface: A diversity training course on a delicate subject that everyone wants to get through quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'covered': ground covered at speed by horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A racecourse is the track that horses gallop round, distance meant to be run in the quickest time.

clue.text: Undeserving rich in Grease — The Musical

parts.note: fat is grease
Cats is the Andrew Lloyd Webber musical

explanation.surface: Wealthy idlers appear in a production of the musical Grease.
explanation.walkthrough: Grease is itself a musical, which tempts one to read the phrase as one title; it splits into a synonym and another show.
explanation.definitionFit: Fat cats are wealthy, overpaid people, especially executives, seen as not earning their riches.

clue.text: With due respect, improperly harassed

indicators.note: something done improperly is done wrongly, so the letters are set out in a wrong order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone protests that, for all the polite 'with due respect', they were badly harassed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With due respect' reads as a stock phrase, but 'With' is only a link and the other two words are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To persecute is to hound or harass someone persistently, so persecuted and harassed are synonyms.

clue.text: Uncomfortable result of checking the small print?

definitions.text: Uncomfortable result of checking the small print?

parts.note: surface reading: scrutinising the hidden terms of a contract, which may bring an unpleasant surprise
setter's reading: physically reading tiny type tires the eyes

explanation.walkthrough: Small print suggests contract terms with nasty catches, but the discomfort is literal, from peering at tiny letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Peering at tiny lettering for long causes tired, aching eyes, the condition named by the answer.

clue.text: Drain the last from capacious jug

indicators.note: the last from means the final character taken out of the word

parts.note: final letter of capacious
a ewer is a large jug

explanation.surface: An order to empty the last of a big jug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drain' reads as a verb for emptying the jug, but it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A sewer is an underground drain carrying waste water.

clue.text: Kind business partner broken by strong emotion

parts.note: Co. is short for company, a business

indicators.note: something broken by another is split open with the other placed in the gap

parts.note: a mate is a partner
passion is strong feeling

explanation.surface: A gentle business partner falls apart under strong feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind' looks like a noun meaning a sort, but it is the adjective; the business and partner are joined first and the emotion breaks into them.
explanation.definitionFit: A compassionate person feels sympathy for others, which is to be kind.

clue.text: Appliance secure in upturned barrel

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other word
upturned in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters run from bottom to top

parts.note: a butt is a large barrel
to secure a prize is to win it

explanation.surface: Something being fastened inside an overturned barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: A twin tub is an old-style washing machine with separate tubs for washing and spinning.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin tub is a domestic washing machine, a household appliance.

clue.text: A brickie's tool turning up in Arab city

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means flipped to run upward, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: A plus hod, the trough a brickie uses to carry bricks

explanation.surface: A bricklayer's hod is found in a Gulf city.
explanation.walkthrough: A brickie is a bricklayer; a hod is the open box on a pole for carrying bricks.
explanation.definitionFit: Doha is the capital city of Qatar, on the Arabian Gulf.

clue.text: Man's regularly thrown out of trading vessel that is for special group

indicators.note: thrown out of means expelled from, so the chosen letters are removed from the word that follows

parts.note: a coaster is a ship trading along the coast

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the word is taken

parts.note: second and fourth letters of the word
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A sailor is thrown off a merchant ship, apparently on behalf of some exclusive clique.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking A and S out of COASTER leaves COTER, and the abbreviation for 'that is' finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small exclusive circle of people sharing an interest, a select group.

clue.text: Money and a girlfriend leading to success: that'll start you off

parts.note: the ready is slang for cash
a steady is a regular girlfriend or boyfriend
to make a go of something is to succeed

explanation.surface: Cash and a steady partner bring success, getting you going in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The ready' is British slang for money; the definition is the starter's call at a race.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the call given to start a children's race, so it literally sets you off running.

clue.text: Weedy wife, mischievous

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for wife
impish means playfully mischievous

explanation.surface: A description of a feeble, naughty wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weedy' looks like an adjective for the wife, but it is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Weedy, of a person, means feeble and lacking strength or spirit, the same as wimpish.

clue.text: One stroke of a Chinese brush perhaps has a role to play

definitions.text: One stroke of a Chinese brush perhaps
definitions.meaning: first, cryptic meaning: one stroke is a component of a written Chinese symbol
second meaning: an acting role portraying a distinctive, often eccentric person

explanation.surface: A calligrapher's single brushstroke is given its own part in a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the first half is a part of a character, since Chinese characters are built from brushstrokes.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre, a character part is a supporting role playing an unusual or eccentric person rather than a lead.

clue.text: Spectacularly bright prosecutor is into white-collar crime: two leaders dismissed

indicators.note: something going into another is placed inside it
the first pair of letters at the head of the word are sent away

parts.note: embezzling is a classic office crime
DA is a District Attorney, a US prosecutor

explanation.surface: A dazzling prosecutor takes on a fraud case, while two bosses are sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: DA, a District Attorney, is the American prosecutor; 'leaders' are the opening letters of the crime, not company bosses.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedazzling means dazzling so brilliantly as to overwhelm, spectacularly bright.

clue.text: Retract one conclusion from jury on appeal

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another is placed after it

parts.note: 'un is a dialect form of one, as in 'a good 'un'
SA is short for sex appeal

indicators.note: 'conclusion from' keeps only the last letter of 'jury'

parts.note: final letter of jury

explanation.surface: A juror withdraws their verdict when the case goes to the appeal court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On appeal' looks like legal language, but it means the jury's last letter goes after SA.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsay something is to take back or withdraw a statement, which is to retract it.

clue.text: Recommended Victoria's first two letters carry a Penny Black

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it within, so one group of letters sits inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
d was the abbreviation for an old British penny

indicators.note: the opening pair of characters of the name is all that is kept

parts.note: the opening two letters of the name
sable is black in heraldry and poetry

explanation.surface: Queen Victoria's initials stamped on the Penny Black, the famous first postage stamp.
explanation.walkthrough: The grammar is loose: the letters from 'a Penny Black' carry Victoria's pair, not the other way round. The Penny Black was Britain's first postage stamp, bearing Victoria's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Something advisable is sensible and to be recommended, so the words are near synonyms.

clue.text: Envy terms hammered out by these old parish workers

indicators.note: terms hammered out are reshaped by hard bargaining, so the letters are beaten into a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Jealous conditions thrashed out by a parish committee of old.
explanation.definitionFit: Vestrymen were members of a parish vestry, the body that ran local church and civil affairs.

clue.text: Between houses note dreadfully small intervals

indicators.note: done dreadfully means done badly, so the letters come out jumbled
something between the two halves is set inside them

parts.note: semis are semi-detached houses, a British staple
the four letters of note rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician practising between houses hits a note dreadfully.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi is a semi-detached house, one of a pair sharing a wall; the reworked note goes inside the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: A semitone is the smallest interval in Western music, half a whole tone.

clue.text: Area between two marks needing a cosmetic

indicators.note: something between two others sits in the gap separating them

parts.note: M for the old German mark, and a scar, a mark on the skin
A is the abbreviation for area
taken as written

explanation.surface: A blemished patch between two spots that calls for some make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: The two marks are different: M is the abbreviation for the German currency, and a scar is a mark left by a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascara is make-up applied to darken eyelashes, a cosmetic.

clue.text: Last in a sequence of home games

indicators.note: of means taken from, so the letters are drawn from inside the words that follow

parts.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: The final fixture in a run of home matches.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final letter of the Greek alphabet, hence the last of any sequence, as in alpha and omega.

clue.text: Turn out, performing for team

parts.note: to evert is to turn inside out
on stage means performing

explanation.surface: Turning out to play for the side.
explanation.walkthrough: Everton is a Premier League football club from Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: Everton is a football club, so the name stands for a team.

clue.text: Her walk amazes, wiggling in this?

definitions.text: Her walk amazes, wiggling in this?

indicators.note: wiggling means moving about from side to side, so the letters are shifted out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An onlooker admires a woman's swaying walk and wonders what outfit she has on.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a woman wearing the garment, while its first three words are rearranged to spell it.
explanation.definitionFit: The shalwar kameez is a South Asian outfit of loose trousers and a long tunic, worn by women walking in it.

clue.text: Announcing consumer magazine that used to be burned

indicators.note: announcing means saying out to listeners, so the word's sound is what counts

parts.note: Which? is the British consumer magazine that tests products

explanation.surface: Declaring that a shopping magazine was once put on the bonfire.
explanation.walkthrough: Which? is the UK's consumer-test magazine. The definition is a relative clause standing for a noun, which troubled the blogger.
explanation.definitionFit: Women accused of witchcraft were historically burned at the stake.

clue.text: Successfully go with this fringe

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to go off with one is to be a great success
second meaning: hair cut straight across the forehead, in American usage

explanation.walkthrough: The first part rests on the idiom 'go with a ...', meaning to succeed in fine style.
explanation.definitionFit: The word completes the idiom for a spectacular success and is also the US term for a hair fringe.

clue.text: Almost everyone in some way can be a chemist perhaps

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the shortened word sits within the next one

parts.note: any can mean some, as in 'have you any?'

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: everyone is all
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A claim that nearly anybody can, by one means or another, become a chemist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In some way' reads as one adverbial phrase, but it splits into a container indicator, 'some' and 'way'.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemist who determines the make-up of substances is an analyst, one example among many kinds.

clue.text: Conductors putting energy into Mass, a long piece with no piano

indicators.note: putting one thing into others sets it inside them
with no means lacking, so the named letter is removed

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mass in physics
taken as written
E is the symbol for energy
a strip is a long narrow piece
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Choirmasters add vigour to a lengthy Mass setting that has no piano part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' with its capital looks like the church service but is just the physics symbol; the second 'a' joins STRIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestri is the Italian plural of maestro, a title for eminent orchestral conductors.

clue.text: Player, good memory, given work to get sharper

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
RAM is computer memory, random-access memory
op. is short for opus, a work
to hone is to sharpen

explanation.surface: A sportsman with a fine memory is given training to make him sharper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' suggests a sportsman, but it is a record player.
explanation.definitionFit: A gramophone is an old-fashioned machine for playing records, a record player.

clue.text: Hitch small horse

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: An instruction to harness a pony to a cart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hitch' reads as a verb for harnessing the horse, but it is the noun meaning a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitch is a minor obstacle or problem, which is what a snag is.
